goal: Checks pipeline health each day: failing builds, flaky tests, queue time, with the day-on-day change.
use: Checks pipeline health each day: failing builds, flaky tests, queue time, with the day-on-day change. Use when checking pipeline health each day.
prompt: Use the rlm-devops-pipeline-health skill on the records for this review.
input: The records for this review, as text or CSV
output: A draft report: findings with location, fix and a not-checked list
pros: Flags a failure rate above 10 percent for a pipeline in the day, a queue time above the target, and a test that passes and fails on the same commit.
cons: Not checked: Failures outside the export.

steps.note: Inspect. The records in scope are listed, and any skipped file is reported.
Partition. The records are cut into chunks, each read on its own.
Map. Each chunk is checked against this skill's rules, one chunk at a time.
Rank. Each pipeline is placed by its failure rate and its queue time.
Verify. Each cited line is re-read, and a finding that does not hold is dropped.
Report. Status: draft for the owner to review. It is not a decision.

findings.title: Queue time 14 minutes against a target of 5
findings.fix: Add runners or split the job

findings.title: Test passes and fails on the same commit
findings.fix: Quarantine the test and fix it

protocol.title: Inspect
protocol.text: The corpus is the generic corpus (docs/SKILL-TEMPLATE-STANDARD.md, section 6): prepare `<input>` with the files in scope, as text. Convert any Excel or PDF input to CSV first (export each sheet as CSV; export PDF tables as CSV or text). Text inputs (CSV, TXT, Markdown) are used as they are. Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py scan <input>`. Note the file count, line count and top-level folders. If the corpus is very large, agree the scope with the user, then narrow it with `--include '<folder>'` (repeatable) on every command. Files over 20 MB are skipped; `--max-bytes N` changes the limit. Report what `scan` lists as skipped.

protocol.title: Partition
protocol.text: Run `WORK=$(mktemp -d)`, then `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py chunk <input> "$WORK/chunks"`. Chunks are limited to 800 lines and 100,000 characters each, and are cut between definitions where possible. Each `chunk_NNN.md` holds the data notice and labelled file sections. `manifest.json` lists the chunks.

protocol.title: Map
protocol.text: For each chunk, run a fresh sub-task (a subagent if you can start one) that sees only that chunk file and the "Chunk task" below. It writes `"$WORK/out/<chunk>.out.md"`. If you cannot start sub-tasks, run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py pending "$WORK/chunks" "$WORK/out"`. It lists the chunks that still have no output. Process the first one: read it, write its output, then run `pending` again. Repeat until nothing is pending. Never hold all chunks in context at once.

protocol.title: Reduce
protocol.text: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py merge "$WORK/out" --out "$WORK/merged.json"`. If it lists `failed_outputs`, re-run those chunks. A missing or invalid output is not "no findings". Checks that span files are done on the merged list in this step. If the merged list is still too large to read, repeat steps 2 to 4 on the findings.

protocol.title: Verify
protocol.text: Recompute each rate from the runs.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: Write the report in the format below.

protocol.title: Clean up
protocol.text: Delete `$WORK` after the report is delivered.
